title: Megaphones and an early television tip in South Bend
summary: No microphones, only megaphones; a stranger in South Bend foretold television around 1933-34.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: No microphones. We used to use the old megaphones. Sing through the megaphone. This old long horn looking thing. Oh, yeah. Wasn't any microphones. Till later on, later. I was playing in South Bend, Indiana. And a fellow came up to me and he said, man, he says, there's something coming out real soon that I sure would like to see you get on. And I'm going to try to help you. And it was television. When was that? This must have been about 33 or 34. It was in its infancy.

Yeah. And this guy, he could foretell that this was going to be a tremendous deal. And he says, with that band you have here, it'd be tremendous. But it never, to me, went in one hand and came out the other. Because to me, the guy was just talking out of his hat to be talking. Which a lot of times people do. But this time, it was actually something to listen to.

Well, I remember, I think it was 39, I saw television at the World's Fair in New York. And I didn't think anything about it. I thought, you know, as a kid, this is just another scientific wonder and you don't pay much attention to.
Well, that's just how to do it. With a grain of salt.
So, you know, nothing's ever going to happen to it. It's very interesting and all that. But, well, I don't think I even understood it at that age.
No, no, no. About 12 years old. Well, that's right.
I didn't have any idea what, well, nobody understood what the future was on.
Right, well, how could you go that far in the advanced days there?
